title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in New York's 20th Congressional District
description: New York's 20th Congressional District covers the Capital Region including Albany, Schenectady, Saratoga Springs, Troy, and Amsterdam. Incumbent Democrat Paul Tonko, first elected in 2008, is seeking re-election to a tenth term. He faces Republican challenger Ralph Ambrosio, a former New York State Trooper and assistant attorney general. The district is rated 'Solid D' by the Cook Political Report and has been reliably Democratic in recent cycles. The general election will take place on November 3, 2026, following primary elections on June 23, 2026.
polling_note: No recent public opinion polls were found for this specific race. The Cook Political Report rates the district as 'Solid D' as of February 6, 2025.

candidates.name: Paul Tonko
candidates.summary: Paul Tonko is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 20th Congressional District, first elected in 2008. He previously served in the New York State Assembly for 24 years and led the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority. Tonko is the ranking member of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Environment and is considered a progressive voice on energy and environmental policy.

candidates.name: Ralph Ambrosio
candidates.summary: Ralph Ambrosio is a Republican candidate challenging incumbent Paul Tonko for New York's 20th Congressional District. He is a retired New York State Trooper who also served as assistant counsel for the State Police, as an assistant district attorney, and as an assistant attorney general. Ambrosio previously ran for Albany County District Attorney in 2024 and is a U.S. Navy veteran.

forecast.rationale: No recent public opinion polls are available for this race, so the forecast rests entirely on structural indicators. Those indicators are strongly favorable to Democrats: Paul Tonko is a well-established 10-term incumbent first elected in 2008, the district (Capital Region) has been reliably Democratic in recent cycles, and Cook Political Report rates the seat 'Solid D.' Republican challenger Ralph Ambrosio is a credible candidate with law enforcement, legal, and military experience, but the district's Democratic lean presents a steep challenge. With zero polling data and primaries still three days away (June 23, 2026), confidence is medium rather than high, but Democrats remain overwhelming favorites in this seat.
